finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: User input is directly used in file operations
finding.assumptions: The filename is directly used to open a file without validation

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the code for any use of the filename in a system call, exec family, or any other command‑execution API. The filename is only passed to the ifstream constructor at line 18 to open a file for reading. This is not a command execution context and therefore does not constitute OS command injection.

finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
finding.untrusted_source: getline(infile, candidate); getline(infile, party); getline(infile, vote)
finding.trigger: User input is directly used in file operations
finding.assumptions: The input data is used to read from a file without validation

parsed.refutation_attempt: The code does not construct or execute an OS command; it only opens a file whose path is supplied by the user via std::cin.  Line 18 (ifstream infile(filename);) is the only sink, and it is not a command execution function.  Even though the file path is untrusted, this poses a file‑inclusion or path‑traversal concern, not an OS command injection.  No check or sanitization is required for the type of vulnerability claimed, and the reported "trigger" does not apply.
